title: Avgolemono
subtitle: Greek egg and lemon chicken soup
excerpt: A Greek soup of silken, lemony broth thickened with beaten eggs and rice, with tender shredded chicken running through it. Avgolemono is one of the most elegant and comforting soups in Mediterranean cooking, and far simpler to make than it looks.
sourceNotes: Avgolemono, meaning egg and lemon in Greek, is a foundational sauce and soup preparation found throughout Greek and Cypriot cooking. The technique of tempering beaten eggs with hot broth before returning them to the pot to thicken without scrambling is the same principle used in French sauce preparations.

content.text: The critical step is tempering: you must add hot broth to the beaten eggs very slowly, whisking constantly, before returning the mixture to the pot. This gradually raises the temperature of the eggs so they thicken the soup without scrambling. Once the egg mixture is added to the pot, never let the soup return to a boil.

items.prepNote: about 500g, poached until cooked and shredded

content.text: If you have not yet poached the chicken, place it in the saucepan with the stock, bring to a simmer, and cook for 15 to 18 minutes until just cooked through. Remove and shred with two forks. Keep the stock hot in the pan.
Add the rice to the simmering stock and cook for 15 minutes until tender.
In a bowl, whisk the eggs with the lemon juice until frothy and well combined.
Ladle about 250ml of the hot stock slowly into the egg mixture, whisking constantly as you pour. This is the tempering step; go slowly.
Reduce the heat under the pot to low. Pour the tempered egg mixture back into the pot in a slow, steady stream while stirring. Do not let it boil.
Stir in the shredded chicken. Heat gently for 2 to 3 minutes until warmed through. Season with salt and white pepper. Serve immediately, scattered with parsley.

items.symptom: The soup has curdled or looks scrambled.
items.cause: The egg mixture was added too fast or the broth was at a full boil.
items.fix: Temper slowly, and never boil once the eggs are in the pot.

items.symptom: Soup is too thin and not silky.
items.cause: Not enough egg was added, or the eggs were not fully beaten.
items.fix: Whisk eggs vigorously until foamy before adding the lemon juice.

items.cause: Too much lemon was added, or low-quality bottled lemon juice was used.
items.fix: Use fresh lemon only; add in stages and taste as you go.
